title: Miren Runtime accepts unverified TLS identities as cluster superusers
summary: The RPC listener requests client certificates without validating their chain. A forged certificate receives an identity that bypasses cluster authorization.

severity.rationale: Unauthenticated callers can obtain full control of applications, sandboxes and cluster resources. The explicit documented impact is control-plane compromise and credential risk.

exposure: Any party reaching the RPC listener can present a self-signed certificate. Restricting network access reduces reach but does not fix certificate verification.

params.instructions: Check miren.dev/runtime version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.11.1 or later. Follow Miren guidance to redeploy applications and rotate credentials referenced in environment variables.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
